original_question: Does there exist, in ZFC, an uncountable set of reals satisfying S_1(B_Γ, B), meaning that for every sequence of countable Borel γ-covers one can choose one set from each cover so that the chosen sets form a countable Borel cover?
target_in_paper: Section 6.2 (The Borel case), Problem 4: Does there exist (in ZFC) an uncountable set of reals satisfying S_1(B_Γ, B)?
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the paper's target property S_1(B_Γ, B), keeps the scope to uncountable sets of reals, asks for a ZFC example rather than a consistency result under extra axioms, and gives the right informal operational reading of S_1 as selecting one member from each Borel γ-cover so that the selections still cover.
missing_details: The underlying object should be named explicitly as a set X ⊆ R, and the covers should be covers of that same X.
The notation S_1(U,V) should be stated in full: for every sequence (U_n)_{n in N} with each U_n in U, there exist U_n in U_n such that {U_n : n in N} is in V.
The paper's convention that a cover is nontrivial is omitted: U is a cover of X only when X = ⋃U and X is not itself a member of U.
The exact meaning of γ-cover should be made explicit: the cover is infinite, and every x in X belongs to all but finitely many members of the cover.
The symbols B_Γ and B should be unpacked as the families of countable Borel γ-covers of X and countable Borel covers of X, respectively.
The draft does not mention the equivalent reformulation recorded in the paper, namely the version about Borel images of uncountable sets of reals dominating N^N.
refined_question: Is there, provably in ZFC and without additional set-theoretic hypotheses, an uncountable set of reals X ⊆ R such that X satisfies S_1(B_Γ, B); that is, for every sequence (U_n)_{n in N} of members of B_Γ(X), where each U_n is a countable nontrivial Borel γ-cover of X, one can choose U_n in U_n for each n so that {U_n : n in N} is a countable nontrivial Borel cover of X?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as stated in the paper: Is it consistent that every uncountable set of reals can be mapped by a Borel function onto a dominating subset of N^N (with domination taken with respect to eventual dominance <=*)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact official formulation given as Problem 4 in Section 6.2, not at a broader neighboring question. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the earlier definitions of S_1(U,V), of nontrivial covers and γ-covers, and of the Borel cover classes B and B_Γ, together with the paper's standing convention that the spaces under discussion are sets of reals unless otherwise indicated. The alternate formulation about Borel images dominating N^N is explicitly recorded immediately after Problem 4, so it is the only paper-backed reformulation worth adding.
